hook: Takeo Kanade earned his PhD in electrical engineering from Kyoto University in 1974 and taught there before joining Carnegie Mellon University in 1980. He directed Carnegie Mellon's Robotics Institute from 1992 to 2001 and now holds the title of U.A. and Helen Whitaker University Professor of Robotics and Computer Science there. Across a research career spanning computer vision and robotics, he pioneered early facial recognition methods, multi-baseline stereo vision, the factorization method for recovering 3D shape and motion from images, and virtualized reality techniques for capturing 3D scenes from multiple cameras. He also led Carnegie Mellon's Navlab autonomous vehicle program, including a 1995 cross-country demonstration drive in which the vehicle steered itself for most of the route from Pittsburgh to San Diego. In 2016 he received the Kyoto Prize in Advanced Technology for his contributions to the field.
